column1: In addition, the financial system allows savers to reduce their risk by spreading their wealth across many different businesses. Larry knows that buying stock in Patti’s doll venture is risky, so he would be smart to use only some of his savings to buy stock in her business. He could also buy stock from his friend Steve, who is opening an ice-cream store. And he could buy stock in established companies, such as IBM, General Electric, and Exxon. Because the success of Patti’s doll venture is not perfectly correlated with the success of Steve’s ice-cream store, or with the profitability of IBM, General Electric, and Exxon, Larry reduces the overall risk he faces when he spreads his wealth around. Reducing risk by holding many imperfectly correlated assets is called diversification.
